## About

Aditi Singh’s Agentic RAG systematizes the integration of autonomous reasoning and planning with retrieval-augmented generation to improve LLM reliability. She is an Assistant College Lecturer at Cleveland State University and an IEEE Senior Member who serves as the researcher lead for Women in AI USA. Her work centers on agentic workflows and interoperability, exemplified by a survey of Model Context Protocol and other communication standards for the Agentic Web. Singh also evaluates the utility of LLMs for specialized tasks such as text-to-SQL generation, prompt engineering, and clinical decision support. She earned her PhD in computer science from Kent State University and previously held roles at MathWorks and Cognizant. In addition to her research, she chairs the Cleveland ACM-W and mentors senior design projects on automated reasoning and verification.

## About

Aditi Singh’s Agentic RAG systematizes the integration of autonomous reasoning and planning with retrieval-augmented generation to improve LLM reliability. She is an Assistant College Lecturer at Cleveland State University and an IEEE Senior Member who serves as the researcher lead for Women in AI USA. Her work centers on agentic workflows and interoperability, exemplified by a survey of Model Context Protocol and other communication standards for the Agentic Web. Singh also evaluates the utility of LLMs for specialized tasks such as text-to-SQL generation, prompt engineering, and clinical decision support. She earned her PhD in computer science from Kent State University and previously held roles at MathWorks and Cognizant. In addition to her research, she chairs the Cleveland ACM-W and mentors senior design projects on automated reasoning and verification.
